newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-SRINATH SET TO RETURN FOR TESTS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRINATH SET TO RETURN FOR TESTS.

text.p: Indian pace bowler Javagal Srinath said on Tuesday he was ready to return to international cricket after being sidelined for five months with a shoulder injury.
"I have been bowling full steam for four days and there's no pain anymore," he said.
Srinath told reporters in the southern city of Bangalore that he wanted to test his shoulder in match play before finalising his comeback to the international arena.
"I need to test my shoulder in actual match conditions which I shall be doing in a local tournament here early next month," he said. "Only then will I know my condition fully.
"Coming back from an injury, I do not want to rush into anything."
Srinath underwent surgery after having to return home from the tour of West Indies in March without having bowled a ball when his injury resurfaced.

Srinath's shoulder problem began last season and forced him to miss the one-off test against Australia in New Delhi. His problem was diagnosed as a rotatory cuff tear and he underwent an operation in May.
"It's too early to know if the shoulder can stand the strain of bowling in a match," Srinath said. "I need to get back into my rhythm.
"I have been bowling for the past few days and am gradually working on my pace. But the big moment will be when I actually bowl in a match next month."
Srinath said he had suffered shooting pains during January's tour of South Africa but went on the West Indies tour before his medical examination report had arrived.
"When I was informed that the injury was serious, I pulled out of the tour," he said.
"Hopefully, there will be no effect on my bowling action," said Srinath, who blossomed into a world-class bowler after training under former Australian pacer Dennis Lillee.
Before the shoulder injury disrupted his career, Srinath had claimed 92 wickets in 27 test matches and dismissed 158 batsmen in 122 one-day internationals.
